source_note: the reference shows no deer: it is only the dark pine forest edge whose palette and evening light the deer must match; draw one deer and nothing else, no trees, no figures
design: slender red deer doe with a warm russet-brown coat, a paler fawn belly, throat and inner legs, a cream rump patch and short white-edged tail, large dark eyes, big upright ears, a dark wet nose, thin legs with small dark hooves, no antlers
view_pose: Whole animal from the tips of its ears down to its hooves, standing square on all four hooves in a neutral alert pose, head level, short tail held down, nothing cropped; the spine points exactly along the view direction, so in a front or back view the body is foreshortened straight behind the head with the two front legs side by side and symmetric, not turned three-quarter, and in a profile view the spine runs exactly sideways
gait: Calm steady deer walk on the spot, one full stride a second: legs lifting high and delicately in turn, all four legs clearly alternating, back level, head held up and level, slight body bob; its body never moves forward
attack: lowers its head and neck down to graze the grass right at its front hooves, nibbling, then lifts its head back up to the start pose; all four hooves stay planted on the same spot
death: startles and drops: its legs fold under it and it sinks down onto its belly and then onto its side on the exact spot where it stood, head resting on the ground, legs stretched out; it never leaps or springs

_note: Wild animal 1 (docs/ART-REDO.md section 10): the deer. The concept paintings have no animal, so the concept crop is the theme.jpg forest edge at the lower left (palette and light only) and the source_note says so; the design text carries the look. Quadruped like the wolf, so it reuses the wolf's view_pose and turntable layout. World height 22 (ears to hooves, a little taller than the wolf's 18, under a hero's 32) is 60 px at the hero texel; side-on about 110 px nose to tail, so the 128 hero cell. Clips: walk x8, idle (the attack slot: head down grazing, back up) x8, death (flee is not a clip kind yet: open question). check anchors come after the views, from `hero_sprites.py deer colours` (the concept crop has no deer colours to anchor). view-S take 1 came out three-quarter twice (head to the camera, flank to screen-right; kept in /workspace/lk/deer-viewS-take1): view_notes.S is the boss's take-3 square-front wording, describing only what a front view shows (face, chest, front legs side by side, hind legs peeking behind) and never the flank, and view_pose no longer asks for all four legs visible.

view_notes.S: Seen exactly from the front, not three-quarter like a deer standing side-on: like looking at a deer walking straight at you, its head points straight at the camera with both of its eyes and both ears equally visible, and the face, neck and chest are square and symmetric about the image's vertical centre line. Only the front of the face, the throat and the chest show; the body is completely hidden straight behind the chest. The two front legs stand side by side, symmetric, and the two hind legs only just peek out behind them

check._note: Tuned on the take-1 trial build (/workspace/lk/deer-clips-take1/trial-sheet.png). anchors: the concepts have no deer, so the anchors are the main colours of the deer's own sheet palette (the russet coat and its shade, the dark brown of hooves, nose and eyes, the near-black, the cream and fawn of the throat, belly and rump); they pin the palette to the approved views, not to a concept. roles: pale is any colour lighter than 0.45 (cream throat, belly, rump patch), dark any colour under 0.2, coat the rest. prop: null. bounds: walking, S shows 33-83 pale px and N 4-17, but the grazing idle (the attack rows) breaks every colour split: head down, S hides its throat (pale 4-20) and N raises its cream rump into view (pale up to 43, and into the head band, 15-17). So the back ceiling is the head band's pale at N's maximum (17; S walk frames 5-45, start 18), and the front floor is S's grazing low point (4). Both are weak: open question 21.

walk-N.gait: Calm steady deer walk on the spot, one full stride a second: legs lifting high and delicately in turn, all four legs clearly alternating, back level, head and ears held high at exactly the same height in every frame, never dipping or nodding, no body bob; its body never moves forward

death-S.struck: It is struck down where it stands: all four hooves stay planted on the ground line until the legs fold, it does not rear, hop, jump, lift its front legs or rise up at any moment;
death-S.death: its front knees buckle first so its chest drops straight down, then its hind legs fold and it sinks onto its belly and settles there on the exact spot where it stood, lying folded with its legs tucked under it and its head resting on the ground between its front knees; it does not roll over or slide toward the camera, no part of it moves closer to the camera or below the line its hooves stood on; it only ever moves downward

death-N.struck: It is struck down where it stands: its hooves never leave the ground, it does not rear, jump or lift its front legs;
death-N.death: its legs fold under it and it sinks down onto its belly and then onto its side on the exact spot where it stood, head resting on the ground, legs stretched out; it never leaps or springs
